text:
Alice: quick flag — we got two reports where queries like `/v1/models?version=beta` end up routed to the stable model. looks like the gateway is dropping or normalizing the `version` query param. anyone seen this before?
Ben: ah. we added a sweeping query-strip rule last year to remove tracking params (utm_*, fbclid) at the edge. could be too greedy.
Priya: I traced it to the rewrite plugin: rule `strip_unknown_query_params` uses `exclude_list` but our regex was `^[a-z_]+$` which accidentally matched `version`. oops.
Marco: that's scary. two immediate concerns: 1) correctness (wrong model selected), 2) cache key mismatch/cache poisoning if some requests are served after rewrite.
Alice: suggested fix: narrow the strip to explicit whitelist of param patterns, and add an allowlist for service-handled params like `version`, `model`, `env`. also we should add a dry-run mode so we can preview effects in Console before flipping. :eyes:
Priya: proposed rule snippet (gateway DSL) — example: 
```yaml
- id: strip-analytics-params
  match: path_prefix: /v1
  queries: 
    strip: ["^utm_.*$", "^fbclid$"]
    preserve: ["^version$", "^model$", "^env$"]
  dry_run: true
```
Ben: +1 to dry_run. also need a unit test harness that simulates both normal and percent-encoded queries (e.g., `%2F`, plus repeated params). path normalization edge cases: trailing slash, `//`, and encoded vs raw.
Marco: agree. also want to normalize percent-encoding (RFC 3986) so `/foo%2Fbar` vs `/foo/bar` are handled consistently for routing, but be careful with path params used by services. maybe offer `path_normalization: strict|relaxed` per-route.
Priya: on headers — we've had internal requests where the gateway injected `x-internal-source: gateway-canary` for canaries. question: should we allow header overrides from rewrite rules or only inject additive headers? security team prefers not to allow overriding `Authorization` or `Host`.
Ben: do not allow `Authorization`, `Host`, `X-Forwarded-For` overrides. we can add `override_blacklist: [Authorization, Host, X-Forwarded-For]` to the DSL.
Alice: example header rule i propose: 
```yaml
- id: canary-inject
  match: route: /v1/generate
  headers:
    add: {"x-candidate-version": "beta-2026-03-10"}
    remove: ["x-dev-debug"]
    allow_override: false
```
Marco: also add an `audit` flag that logs original vs rewritten headers/queries (redact auth tokens) and emits metrics: `rewrite.applied`, `rewrite.skipped`, `rewrite.failed`, and `rewrite.duration_ms`. this will help correlate customer bugs.
Priya: telemetry proposal: emit counter + sample traces with tags `{rule_id, route, outcome, user_tier}`, and histogram of latency. set default sampling for rewrites to 1% but increase to 100% for errors.
Ben: caching note: cache key must include a `rewrite_hash` or canonical query string after rewrite. otherwise two different original queries could map to same backend but wrong cache entry. add a `cache.rewrite_safe: true/false` flag per-rule.
Alice: UX: Console should show a live preview (input request) -> transformed request, with a toggle to run in `dry-run` (log only) and an excerpt of sampled telemetry for the rule. rollout plan: dry-run -> canary 10% -> 100% with 30m watch window + automatic rollback on rewrite.error > 0.1%
Marco: rollout automation: add constraint that header-injection rules that add `x-internal*` only apply to private/dedicated clusters by default. SaaS tenants shouldn't see internal headers unless explicitly allowed.
Priya: edge-case we found: array query params (e.g., `?tag=a&tag=b`) getting collapsed into `tag=a,b` by the rewrite. preserve multi-valued semantics unless the service expects CSV. add `query_serialization: preserve|csv|repeat` option.
Ben: noted. i'll update the envoy/lua filter to respect `preserve` semantics. will add tests for percent-encoding, repeated params, and multi-values.
Alice: action items: Priya - create test harness + telemetry schema; Ben - patch filter + tests; Marco - console preview + dry-run toggle + rollout UI; Alice - write short doc + changelog entry and runbook for rollback.
deploy-bot: deployment note — canary config for `eng-platform` will include `dry_run` enabled by default. scheduled rollout window: 2026-03-25 02:00 UTC -> 02:30 UTC.
Priya: I'll start a ticket and attach sample requests that triggered the bug. please add any more cases you remember here.
Ben: adding my list: encoded slashes, repeated `version` param, empty-valued params, and `+` vs space encoding in queries.
Alice: thanks all. let's keep the dry-run on until we see zero regressions for 48h. :thumbsup:
